title: Parameter-Efficient Reinforcement Learning using Prefix Optimization
claim: A small trainable adapter writes a solution prefix, a frozen large model completes it, and the reward from the final answer updates only the adapter.
layout: Single loop, left-to-right then right-to-left, dashed text boxes, reward feedback arrow
description: A cyclic flow diagram with a worked math example. At top left, a dashed box holds the prompt "How many divisors does 196 have?". An arrow leads to a pink "Adapter Model (1B params)" box labeled "trained model". A second dashed box shows the prompt plus a short green-highlighted prefix, "## Step 1: To find the number of divisors,". An arrow leads to a blue "Target Model (7B/70B params)" box with a snowflake icon, labeled "inference only". Another arrow goes down to a large dashed box. It shows the green prefix followed by yellow-highlighted completion text, ending in "The final answer is 9". An arrow leads left to a gray "Reward Model" box reading Prediction: 9, Answer: 9, Reward: +1. A curved arrow labeled "Reward for RL update" returns to the adapter. The eye goes first to the colored model boxes, then follows the loop.
caption: An illustration of the Prefix-RL method. A small adapter model receives the input question and generates the first k tokens (prefix) in the response. The large target model is used in “inferencemode” to complete the solution. We then compute the reward based on the final answer generated by the model, and apply standard RL procedure (PPO) to update the adapter model (keeping the target model frozen).
abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a leading approach for tuning language models on mathematical reasoning tasks. However, it remains unclear whether RLVR's gains stem from genuine reasoning improvements or simply from steering the model toward answer formats that already appear in the reference distribution. Inspired by recent evidence \citep{zhao2025echo,yue2025does}, we study this question by optimizing only the first $k$ tokens (e.g. $k=32$) of each solution, generating the remainder of the response from the reference model. We study two methods for prefix optimization, using a naive algorithm that clusters prefixes and selects the best prefix (Prefix Clustering), and a method that optimizes the prefix by finetuning a lightweight adapter model with RL (Prefix-RL). We show that tuning only the first $k$ tokens can significantly improve the accuracy on math, suggesting that at least some of the gains from RL are due to upweighting a preferable solution strategy. Our results suggest that simple prefix optimization methods can provide an efficient alternative to RL, delivering substantial improvements across different models and benchmarks for a tiny fraction of the compute required for standard RL, and that these gains are robust across prefix lengths and random seeds.
